correctness.rationale: The exact size-bias identity follows from multinomial falling-factorial moments, and pairwise midpoint convexity proves the sign for any convex functional. For uniform p the normalized pair-collision statistic is affine to Pearson Q. The discrete one-edge conditional difference equals 4q^2 at zero, 2q(1-q) at ±1, zero elsewhere; symmetry yields the finite formula and positive sign for all n,N. An aperiodic local CLT for n≥3 and a parity-sensitive binomial estimate for n=2 establish the fixed-n cyclic limit 2/sqrt(pi). Independent exact-rational complete finite enumerations in verify_covariance.py pass at all specified sizes.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating literature explicitly contrasts DTV and Pearson goodness-of-fit but calibrates only individual null moments. Their exact positive cross covariance provides nontrivial joint information for ordered histogram goodness-of-fit, and the graph-topology-independence plus bin-count-free cyclic limiting constant exposes a structural feature of multinomial fluctuations. The general unbiased collision identity explains this phenomenon for all convex histogram functionals and nonuniform sampling, beyond routine numerical tabulation.
